verdict.rationale: Entra documents Lifecycle Workflows that automatically run processes against users across the three phases of their lifecycle, which covers joiner/mover/leaver. It also documents automatic outbound provisioning into SaaS and on-premises apps. However, nothing in the pack shows an HRIS acting as the authoritative source that feeds the directory. Missing for 10: documented inbound HR-driven provisioning (an HRIS as source of truth), evidence that HR changes trigger directory and app-assignment updates end to end, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, HR drives identity — the HRIS is the source of truth, and joiner/mover/leaver changes flow into the directory and app assignments automatically

citations.quote: Lifecycle workflows (LCW) are identity governance capabilities that enable organizations to manage Microsoft Entra users across the three phases of a user's lifecycle with an organization
Workflows contain specific processes that run automatically against users as they move through their lifecycle.
Common scenarios include provisioning a Microsoft Entra user into SaaS applications like Dropbox, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and many more.
Microsoft Entra ID also supports provisioning users into applications hosted on-premises or in a virtual machine, without having to open up any firewalls.
